title: Phished HR account used to bulk-download employee PII
threat_event: Attacker phishes an HR specialist with an adversary-in-the-middle kit, captures the session, and exports employee records
vulnerability: Push-based MFA can be relayed by phishing kits; no alert on unusually large record exports
existing_controls: Enterprise SSO with push MFA (inherited); annual awareness training; SOC monitoring
impact_rationale: About 1,200 employees' SSNs, addresses, and pay data; triggers state breach notification and credit monitoring costs
response_plan: Require phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) for HR specialist and HR administrator roles; alert the SOC when one user views or exports more than 50 records in an hour

title: Known flaw in an application dependency exploited from the internet
threat_event: Scanner finds and exploits a published vulnerability in an outdated application library
vulnerability: Two moderate dependency flaws were 78 and 85 days old against a 60-day requirement
existing_controls: Weekly authenticated scans; dependency scan in CI; WAF on load balancer
impact_rationale: Successful exploitation of the web tier could expose the database of employee records
response_plan: Update dependencies in release 2.4 and fail CI builds on findings past their remediation deadline

title: Dormant account used to sign in after the owner left
threat_event: Former contractor or an attacker with leaked credentials signs in to an enabled but inactive account
vulnerability: Six local and service accounts were inactive 41 to 97 days and still enabled; disabling relies on a manual monthly review
existing_controls: SSO deprovisioning for employees; manual monthly account review
impact_rationale: Service accounts reach the database; misuse would expose a subset of records and be hard to attribute
response_plan: Automate disabling at 35 days of inactivity and alert the ISSO on exceptions

title: HR staff member browses or takes coworkers' records
threat_event: An HR specialist views pay or medical-benefit details of coworkers with no business need and copies them
vulnerability: HR roles can view all employee records; access to individual records is logged but not reviewed for patterns
existing_controls: Role-based access; record-access logging; acceptable use agreement
impact_rationale: Privacy harm to a limited number of employees; HR disciplinary and legal exposure
response_plan: Add a SOC alert for record views outside the specialist's assigned employee group and review hits weekly

title: Malicious activity in portal logs goes unnoticed for weeks
threat_event: Attacker activity that SOC correlation rules do not catch sits in portal-specific logs without anyone reviewing them
vulnerability: Weekly ISSO reviews were recorded for only 5 of the last 12 weeks
existing_controls: SOC central alerting on high-severity events; logs retained 12 months
impact_rationale: SOC alerting still covers high-severity events; the gap mainly lengthens detection of low-and-slow misuse
response_plan: Use a recurring review ticket with a checklist so every weekly review leaves a record

title: Breach at the payroll provider exposes Acme pay statements
threat_event: Attacker compromises Bayline Payroll Services and takes pay statement files before or after transfer
vulnerability: Acme relies on contract terms and the vendor's own controls; no independent assurance report has been reviewed this year
existing_controls: PGP-encrypted files over key-based SFTP; ISA-2026-04; contract breach-notification clause
impact_rationale: Pay statements contain names and pay data for all employees; Acme stays accountable to its workforce
response_plan: Obtain and review the vendor's current SOC 2 Type II report; add a 72-hour breach notification and cost-sharing clause at contract renewal

title: Destructive attack or outage leaves the portal unrecoverable
threat_event: Ransomware or a destructive actor encrypts or deletes the portal VMs and database
vulnerability: The contingency plan is approved but has never been tested; restore time is unknown
existing_controls: Managed database point-in-time backups; VM images in the build pipeline
impact_rationale: Availability is categorized LOW; HR can fall back to paper forms and emailed statements for several days
response_plan: Run a tabletop exercise and a database restore test and record the results

title: Document upload bucket accidentally made public
threat_event: An administrator changes the storage bucket policy during troubleshooting and leaves it publicly readable
vulnerability: No guardrail blocks public access at the tenant level; drift would only appear in the monthly configuration scan
existing_controls: Private bucket policy; monthly CIS benchmark scan; change management
impact_rationale: Uploaded documents include tax and benefits forms with SSNs; a public bucket is found by scanners within hours
response_plan: Enable the provider's account-level public access block and add a daily alert on any bucket policy change

title: Traffic intercepted over a weak TLS version
threat_event: Attacker in a privileged network position downgrades a session to TLS 1.0 and reads it
vulnerability: The load balancer accepted TLS 1.0 and 1.1 until the policy was corrected during the assessment
existing_controls: TLS 1.2+ policy applied 2026-10-07; monthly TLS configuration scan
impact_rationale: Exposure would be limited to individual sessions an attacker can position against
response_plan: Accept the residual risk; the monthly TLS scan will detect any regression

title: Benefits carrier certificate expires during open enrollment
threat_event: The mutual TLS certificate for the Harborview Benefits API expires and elections stop transmitting
vulnerability: Certificate expiry dates are tracked in a spreadsheet with no automated reminder
existing_controls: Manual certificate inventory; carrier accepts a late file within 5 business days
impact_rationale: Elections can be resent once the certificate is renewed; HR loses time and employees may see delays
response_plan: Add expiry monitoring with 60-, 30-, and 7-day alerts for every portal certificate

title: HR administrator grants excessive roles by mistake
threat_event: An HR administrator assigns the HR specialist role to the wrong employee during a reorganization
vulnerability: Role changes need no second approval
existing_controls: Quarterly privileged role review; role assignment logging
impact_rationale: The wrong person could view records until the quarterly review catches it
response_plan: Accept; the quarterly role review limits exposure to one quarter. Revisit if HR headcount grows

title: Cloud region outage takes the portal offline
threat_event: A regional failure of IaaS compute or managed database services makes the portal unavailable
vulnerability: The portal runs in a single region
existing_controls: Provider multi-zone deployment within the region; provider SLA
impact_rationale: Availability is categorized LOW and outages of a day or two are tolerable
response_plan: Accept; a second region is not justified for a LOW-availability system

title: Natural disaster destroys a provider site
threat_event: Fire or flood destroys the provider availability zone hosting a portal VM
vulnerability: Inherited physical and environmental protection from the IaaS provider
impact_rationale: The other zone keeps serving; backups are stored in a separate zone
response_plan: Accept; inherited controls and multi-zone design cover this

title: Session hijacked through cross-site scripting
threat_event: Attacker plants a script in a self-service form field to steal another user's session
vulnerability: Input fields are encoded by the framework but no dynamic application scan has been run
existing_controls: Framework output encoding; HttpOnly session cookies; Content Security Policy
impact_rationale: One user's session could be taken over; SSO re-authentication limits the window
response_plan: Add an authenticated dynamic scan before each major release

title: Forged pay statements pushed through the SFTP interface
threat_event: An attacker who steals the payroll provider's SFTP key uploads altered pay statements
vulnerability: The SFTP key is not rotated on a set schedule
existing_controls: Key-based SFTP from a fixed source address; PGP signatures checked on import
impact_rationale: Employees could see wrong pay figures and lose trust in the portal; actual pay is unaffected
response_plan: Accept; signature checks catch altered files. Add key rotation to the next ISA review
